title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: Java fields and enum constants indexed, captured locals resolved
summary: The Java parser gets the same treatment the Kotlin one got in 1.42.17: fields without a modifier, annotations with nested parentheses, enum constants read in full, comments and text blocks kept out of the brace count. Go to Definition no longer lands inside a string or a comment, and resolves a local captured by an anonymous class.

highlights.title: Java fields without a modifier
highlights.description: `@Inject AnalyticsAdapter analytics;`, `@Mock UserRepository repository;` and interface constants were never indexed, and their annotations leaked onto the next method (`@Deprecated String legacy;` struck through the method below). They have an Outline entry, a hover and usages now.

highlights.title: Captured locals resolve
highlights.description: Inside `new View.OnClickListener() { public void onClick(View v) { open(url, title); } }` the parameter and the local of the enclosing method resolved to nothing or to a stranger elsewhere. Same fix for a Kotlin `object : Listener`. A binding sitting inside a string or a comment is no longer a destination.

highlights.title: Enum colours and comments
highlights.description: A nested `enum class State` and every `Foo.State` reference took the enum member colour. Code commented out with a multi-line `/* … */` kept its class and function colours. Both are fixed, and a backtick test name gets one declaration token on the name itself.

sections.heading: Java parser
bullets: Fields without a modifier are indexed at class level; locals inside method bodies stay out.
Same-line annotations with nested parentheses (`@Query("SELECT count(*) …")`) and a package-private `@interface` no longer hide the declaration.
Enum constants are read in full (`Home` was `H`), multi-line arguments and a constructor after `};` are not constants, `@Deprecated OLD,` does not mark the next method.
A `/*` left open, a `/* { */`, a Javadoc `{@code` and the lines of a `"""` text block no longer shift the Outline or produce phantom methods.

sections.heading: Navigation and colours
bullets: Go to Definition ignores a local binding that sits inside a string or a comment (Java and Kotlin).
A local or parameter captured by an anonymous class or a Kotlin `object :` resolves to the enclosing function.
The continuation of a Java ternary (`? format(value)`) is not a method header.
Nested `enum class` painted as enum, no semantic colours inside a multi-line block comment, backtick names get one declaration token.
